title: Finite coefficient coordinates and adjunction transport over an isomorphic projective line
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, n a nonnegative level with finite coefficient quotient A=ULift(O_E/l^(n+1)), and X,S Noetherian schemes. Fix the actual tower base and geometry g for f:X→S, its coefficient pullback cp, and an isomorphism e:X≅P¹_S over S. Assume l is invertible on S. Use the constant- and root-section normalized CoefficientCoordinates [def-sp-p1-coefficient-coordinates] and the fixed-scalar realization [def-sp-finite-intrinsic-direct-adjunction]. There are such coordinates cS,cX, an exponent-unit witness on X, and natural isomorphisms p:F_S L_fin≅p_P¹* H and q:H R_fin≅Rp_P¹* F_S, where H=e* F_X and p_P¹ is the projection. They satisfy the adjunction unit equation for every ordinary derived object. Moreover the evaluated coefficient pullback, followed by the coordinate of the coefficient unit on X, equals L_fin of the coefficient coordinate on S followed by p and the ordinary unit pullback. Coefficient pullbacks and their section normalization are those of [def-sp-tower-class-diagonal]. No Chern data, class, or projective-line splitting is asserted.

proof.text: Construct the normalized constant and Tate-line coordinates on X and S from the constant-sheaf universal property and the root-to-tensor map. On every etale chart and pro-etale refinement they send the scalar a and tensor a⊗z to the identical scalar and tensor; these generators determine the isomorphisms. Pullback from S and the isomorphism e give the exponent-unit witness on X.

Use the section-normalized derived direct-image realization comparison. Transport along e using its inverse-image equivalence and he to identify the geometric projection. Take inverse-image mates to obtain p and q. The adjunction mate unit identity gives the first equation for every derived object.

On coefficient single complexes, the ordinary adjoint of cp.iso has the constant-ring restriction formula by cp.normalization. Every coordinate has that same section formula, so the maps agree on all constants and hence on the sheaf. Exact single-complex localization gives the second equation, with the inverse pullEvaluation on its source.

theorem finiteP1_coefficient_adjunction_coordinates
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian S]
    (b : SpTowerShriek.Base l E) {f : X ⟶ S}
    (e : X ≅ ProjectiveLine S) (he : e.hom ≫ (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) = f)
    (g : SpTowerShriek.Geometry l E b f) (cp : CoefficientPullback l E b f g)
    (hS : IsUnit (l : Γ(S, ⊤))) (n : ℕ) [Finite (SpTowerShriek.R l E n)] :
    let A := FiniteRing l E n
    let F := (Scheme.sfIntrinsicModuleEquivalence S
      (SpTowerShriek.R l E n)).functor.mapDerivedCategory
    let H := finiteOverRealization l E n e
    let L := Scheme.proEtaleConstantRingDerivedPullback (SpTowerShriek.R l E n) f
    let R := (Scheme.proEtaleConstantRingPushforward
      (SpTowerShriek.R l E n) f).rightDerivedFunctor
    let ad := (Scheme.proEtaleConstantRingAdjunction
      (SpTowerShriek.R l E n) f).mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction
    let ap := derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)
    ∃ (hX : IsUnit ((l ^ (n + 1) : ℕ) : Γ(X, ⊤)))
      (cX : SpTowerP1.CoefficientCoordinates l E n X hX)
      (cS : SpTowerP1.CoefficientCoordinates l E n S
        (by simpa only [Nat.cast_pow] using hS.pow (n + 1)))
      (p : F ⋙ L ≅ geoP1Pullback A (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) ⋙ H)
      (q : H ⋙ R ≅ geoP1Pushforward A (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) ⋙ F),
      (∀ M, ad.unit.app (F.obj M) ≫ R.map (p.hom.app M) ≫
        q.hom.app ((geoP1Pullback A (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)).obj M) = F.map (ap.unit.app M)) ∧
      ((g.pullEvaluation n).inv.app (unit S (Arings l E S)) ≫
        (SpTowerShriek.Ev l E X n).map (cp.derivedIso l E).hom ≫
        (finiteOverUnitCoordinate l E n e cX).hom =
      L.map (finiteUnitCoordinate l E n S cS).hom ≫ p.hom.app (geoP1Unit A S) ≫
        H.map (geoP1UnitPullback A (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)).hom)
